# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.

/** Paste lines of claims into the paste box: how many were added, or null when refused. */
export async function pasteClaims(page: Page, text: string): Promise<number | null> {
  // A paste that only updates DRAFTs in place adds no row: the count it shows is the
  // result, judged against the value before the click as countAfter judges it.
  const cell = page.getByTestId('paste-added');
  const before = await claimRows(page).count();
  const was = (await cell.count()) > 0 ? await shown(cell) : '';
  await page.getByTestId('paste-claims').fill(text);
  await page.getByTestId('paste-submit').click();
  let cleared = false;
  const counted = async () => {
    if ((await cell.count()) === 0) return false;
    const now = await shown(cell);
    if (now === '') { cleared = true; return false; }
    return now !== was || was === '' || cleared;
  };
  const ok = await until(page, async () => (await counted()) || (await claimRows(page).count()) > before,
    page.getByTestId('paste-error'), 'paste claims');
  return ok ? Number(await shown(cell)) : null;
}

# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/claims — add a claim to a person (body: {amount,
# date, note, user, corrects}). The amount is required: a number with up to two decimals. A
# negative amount is a correction: corrects must name, by number, a SETTLED claim of the same person
# (refused otherwise); corrects must be blank for any other amount. A blank date takes the sheet's today. Refused (400), storing nothing, when the amount or date is
# not valid, the person is not on the sheet, the date falls in a closed period, or the person is
# retired from a date before it.
# A stored change is recorded in the audit file as CLAIM_ADDED; a refused one records nothing.
validate:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.ValidateClaim
  next: load
load:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.person.LoadPerson
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkDate
checkDate:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.CheckDatePeriod
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkRetired
checkRetired:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.CheckRetired
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkCorrection
checkCorrection:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.CheckCorrection
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: snapshot
snapshot:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.rollup.SnapshotRollup
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.SaveClaimAdded
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit
audit:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.AuditClaimAdded
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.RespondWithClaim
  govern: [ transaction ]
# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/quick-add — add a DRAFT claim for a person by name (body: {name, amount,
# user}), dated the sheet's today with an empty note. A name not on the sheet (ignoring case and the
# spaces around it) adds the person first, with grade A. The person form's and the claim form's
# rules apply: refused (400), storing nothing and recording nothing, when the name is empty, the
# amount is not valid, the sheet's today falls in a closed period, or the named person is retired
# from a date before it. The whole quick add is one
# change: the person is added only once the claim has passed every check.
# Records PERSON_ADDED (and its ROLLUP) for a new person, then CLAIM_ADDED.
validate:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.quick.ValidateQuickAdd
  next: checkDate
checkDate:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.CheckDatePeriod
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: person
person:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.quick.FindOrAddPerson
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: snapshot
snapshot:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.rollup.SnapshotRollup
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.SaveClaimAdded
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit
audit:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.AuditClaimAdded
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.RespondWithClaim
  govern: [ transaction ]
# OfficeFloor REST wiring

Domain REST endpoints are declared here as OfficeFloor YAML, served by the
`officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` inside the Spring Boot host. Put them under `rest/api/` so
their paths start with `/api/` — `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend; a non-`/api/`
path returns the SPA's `index.html` instead of your endpoint. Directory nesting maps to path
segments, so `rest/api/owners.GET.yml` → `GET /api/owners`. Each route is its own file:

```
# officefloor/rest/api/<path>.GET.yml   (or .POST.yml, {param}.GET.yml, ...)
service:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.<SomeLogic>   # a class with a service(...) method
```

The logic class's `service(...)` method takes injected dependencies (Spring `@Service` beans, the
data layer) and a `net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse<T>` to send the response.

(The `/actuator/health` readiness endpoint is Spring-side — Actuator — not an OfficeFloor route.)

# OfficeFloor REST wiring

Domain REST endpoints are declared here as OfficeFloor YAML, served by the
`officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` inside the Spring Boot host. Put them under `rest/api/` so
their paths start with `/api/` — `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend; a non-`/api/`
path returns the SPA's `index.html` instead of your endpoint. Directory nesting maps to path
segments, so `rest/api/owners.GET.yml` → `GET /api/owners`. Each route is its own file:

```
# officefloor/rest/api/<path>.GET.yml   (or .POST.yml, {param}.GET.yml, ...)
service:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.<SomeLogic>   # a class with a service(...) method
```

The logic class's `service(...)` method takes injected dependencies (Spring `@Service` beans, the
data layer) and a `net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse<T>` to send the response.

(The `/actuator/health` readiness endpoint is Spring-side — Actuator — not an OfficeFloor route.)

content.text: Function classes may only have one public method. I'll keep the shared statics package-private and expose them via a small utility class in the claim package.

The paste box is in place, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works**
- You paste lines of `name,amount,date,note`. Each line is split at its first three commas, so the note keeps any commas it holds. A blank date means the sheet's today, and the note can be left off.
- The name has to be a person already on the sheet. Case and spaces around the name are ignored, as elsewhere in the app.
- Every line is checked against the claim form's rules before anything is saved: the amount format, the date, closed periods, and retirement. A negative amount is refused, because a paste line has no field for the claim it would correct.
- If any line fails, the error (with its line number) shows on the box and nothing is stored or written to the audit file. Otherwise each line becomes a DRAFT claim, in order, written as `CLAIM_ADDED` exactly as a single add is.
- The box then shows how many were added. The count disappears while a paste is running.

**What changed**
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{id}/paste-claims`, with its classes in a new `paste/` package.
- **Front end:** a new paste box, `features/claims/paste.slot.tsx`.
- **Existing claim code:** I pulled the claim form's checks, save and audit steps into package-private helpers, and added `claim/ClaimAdding.java` so the paste reuses the same code instead of copying it. This was needed because OfficeFloor refuses to start if one of its step classes has more than one public method.

**Choices to confirm**
- Blank lines in the paste are skipped. A paste with no lines at all is refused.
- A line with fewer than two fields (name and amount) is refused.
- No database change was needed.
